AddText "The link opens onto an argument already in progress. Someone reads your transponder code aloud, and someone else asks - twice, and not calmly - what exactly you thought you were fishing for."
$menuState = fleetConvMain 0

AddText "\"Be advised, the incident has been logged.\" $PersonRank $personName holds up a slate as though you could read it. \"Hull breach, non-standard munition, recovered intact. It is going to Naval Intelligence, because everything unidentified goes to Naval Intelligence. You will be hearing about the barb.\""
$menuState = fleetConvMain 0
FireAll PopulateOptions

AddText "\"Damage assessment is complete and your involvement is not in dispute.\" $PersonRank $personName reads without inflection. \"You will receive a schedule of costs. It will be itemised. One of the items will be the harpoon, which we have kept.\""
$menuState = fleetConvMain 0
FireAll PopulateOptions

AddText "$PersonRank $personName looks at the puncture, then at you, with the particular patience of someone cataloguing a sin. \"A machine for taking things out of the dark,\" $heOrShe says. \"And you pointed it at people.\""
$menuState = fleetConvMain 0
FireAll PopulateOptions

AddText "Whoever answers is laughing. \"It shot a rope at us! A rope!\" The laughing stops very suddenly. \"Do it again and we will come and see what else your ship does.\""
$menuState = fleetConvMain 0
FireAll PopulateOptions

AddText "\"That,\" says $personName, with something close to admiration, \"is not a weapon. That is a fishing rig.\" A pause. \"Which you fired. At us. What is wrong with you?\""
$menuState = fleetConvMain 0
FireAll PopulateOptions

AddText "\"You have discharged an unregistered device at a vessel of the Diktat.\" $PersonRank $personName does not blink. \"I am required to ask whether this was deliberate. I am not required to believe the answer.\""
$menuState = fleetConvMain 0
FireAll PopulateOptions

AddText "\"There is a form for this.\" $PersonRank $personName sounds almost pleased about it. \"There is not a form for this, actually. I have checked. I am going to have to write to someone about the fact that there is no form for this.\""
$menuState = fleetConvMain 0
FireAll PopulateOptions

AddText "\"You put a hook in us,\" says $personName, in the flat voice of somebody who has had a long month and is not going to have a shorter one. \"Not a shot. A hook. We are going to be explaining that to the yard for a year.\""
$menuState = fleetConvMain 0
FireAll PopulateOptions

notes: The patrol sent about a harpooning, arriving. Unprefixed keys because there is no active person at this trigger, which puts the fleet's own memory in the local scope. Marked as had here rather than at each ending, as the cargo scan does: the patrol is still pursuing while the dialog is open, so a conversation that only counted once it was finished would be reopened the instant the player closed it.

text:
"We have a report of a $faction hull holed by - " $PersonRank $personName stops, checks the screen again, and continues in the voice of someone who has decided not to editorialise. " - by a fishing implement."

"Damage to fleet property, discharge of a projectile weapon inside a patrolled lane, and whatever the tribunal decides to call the rest of it. Settle it here for $entity.catchrelease_harpoonFineDGS credits and it goes in the file as an accident."

"Hegemony Navy. Heave to."

$PersonRank $personName works through it without looking up. "Discharge of an unregistered device, damage to a registered hull, and an entry under 'munition, description of' that I have had to write out by hand. The schedule for all three comes to $entity.catchrelease_harpoonFineDGS credits."

$HeOrShe finally looks up. "Pay it and the file says accident. Don't, and it says something else, and then it stops being mine."

"Tri-Tachyon corporate security. This is a billing matter."

$PersonRank $personName has the figure ready. "Hull damage, survey time, and the recovery of a foreign object from a company vessel. $entity.catchrelease_harpoonFineDGS credits, settled now, at the pre-litigation rate."

"The post-litigation rate is not a number I am authorised to say out loud."

"Peace be with you. Cut your engines."

$PersonRank $personName looks tired rather than angry. "A crew of ours has a hole in their ship and a story nobody believes. The Church is not interested in punishing curiosity. It is interested in the repair, which comes to $entity.catchrelease_harpoonFineDGS credits."

"Pay it, and we will both call this a lesson."

"Stop. Stop there."

The voice is young and delighted. "You are the one with the machine that grabs. Everyone has heard. We are not supposed to want to see it."

A cough off-screen, and the delight is packed away. "Tribute for the ship you holed. $entity.catchrelease_harpoonFineDGS credits. Then we look at your gear, and then we decide what it is."

"Hold position, friend."

$PersonName is grinning. "Word is you put a hook in a hull. Not shot it - hooked it. Half of us want to buy you a drink and the other half want the rig."

"Neither's happening. What is happening is $entity.catchrelease_harpoonFineDGS credits, and then nobody has to find out how the rest of it goes."

"Heave to for the Sindrian Diktat."

$PersonRank $personName reads the charge as though it were a sentence. "Discharge of an unregistered device within Diktat space, against a Diktat hull. The administrative penalty is $entity.catchrelease_harpoonFineDGS credits."

"The administrative penalty is the favourable outcome. I would take it."

"Persean League patrol. Cut your drive."

$PersonRank $personName has clearly been reading up. "There is no statute for this. There is a statute for discharging a weapon at a member-state hull, and a separate one for damage caused by recovery equipment, and I have decided to apply both."

"$entity.catchrelease_harpoonFineDGS credits. Argue it with a committee if you like, but not with me."

"Independent patrol. Ease off."

$PersonName sounds like somebody who took this contract for the fuel allowance. "Somebody you hooked filed with us, and filing means I have to fly out here and say a number at you. The number is $entity.catchrelease_harpoonFineDGS credits."

"Say yes and we can both go back to what we were doing."

text: One of the drinkers has a slate out and a list on it, and keeps looking at the door as though expecting somebody who knows what they are doing with a net.

options: catchrelease_standingOrder_ask:Ask about the list.

text:

"$catchreleaseRewardCap, on delivery."
options:
catchrelease_jobAccept:Take the order.
catchrelease_jobDecline:"Not my sort of water."

text: $HeOrShe writes something next to the list without looking up. "It will keep."
The slate goes back to the bar top.

$catchreleaseRewardCap, counted out on the bar top.

options: catchrelease_chef_ask:Ask the cook what the problem is.

text:
"Three things," the cook says, before you have said anything at all. "On one plate. It is $catchreleaseDish and it does not work with two."

"I need $catchreleaseAsk. Not similar. Different. That is the entire idea."

"$catchreleaseRewardCap when they are in my kitchen and not before."
options:
catchrelease_jobAccept:Take the order.
catchrelease_jobDecline:"Find another supplier."

text: "Good. Do not freeze them."
The cook goes back to the comm slate, and back to losing.
"Three," the cook says, without looking up. "$catchreleaseAskCap. It is still three."

The cook unpacks all of it on the bar top, in front of everyone, and spends a long time not saying anything.

"Yes. That is the plate." You are paid $catchreleaseReward, and told to come back in a month, when there will be a different plate.
A young man with a very good jacket and a very cheap drink is explaining something to two people who are not listening, and to a third who left.

options: catchrelease_startup_ask:Let the young man finish his sentence.

text:
"You fish," he says. It is not a question and he does not wait. "Everyone in this sector eats reconstituted protein because nobody has solved logistics. I have solved logistics. What I do not have is a demonstrated inbound."

"$catchreleaseAskCap. That is all. I need to be able to say, truthfully, that it arrived."

"$catchreleaseRewardCap for the first run. There will be more runs."
options:
catchrelease_jobAccept:Agree to the first run.
catchrelease_jobDecline:"No."

text: "Excellent. I will need an invoice. Do you do invoices?"
"That is fine. That is fine. I have other conversations." He does not.
"Still waiting on the inbound," he says, with the brightness of a man who has told somebody a date. "$catchreleaseAskCap."
He counts it twice, photographs it, and pays you $catchreleaseReward without haggling, which from him is alarming.

He is already scrolling. "Right. Right. Now the same again, at volume, because the figure I showed them was not the figure you just delivered."

"$catchreleaseAskCap. Same terms, better terms, whatever you want - I have investors now."
"That is a supply chain," he says, to himself more than to you. "That is a supply chain and I have one."
A man in a plain, expensive coat is not drinking, and has been not drinking for some time. He watches the door the way somebody does when they are being paid to be somewhere.

options: catchrelease_butler_ask:Ask the man in the coat who he is waiting for.

text:
"I am buying for a household," he says. "I will not be naming it."

"The requirement is $catchreleaseAsk. I am told that is a difficult number. I am not empowered to lower it."

His expression does not change. "It is to be looked at, you understand. Not eaten. Whether it is a good specimen of its kind is not a question that has been put to me."

"$catchreleaseRewardCap, on presentation."
options:
catchrelease_jobAccept:Accept the commission.
catchrelease_jobDecline:Leave him to it.

text: "Very good." He writes nothing down, which suggests he does not need to.
"Understood." He resumes not drinking.
"The requirement has not changed," he says. "$catchreleaseAskCap."

He does not look at it for long. He looks at the scale.

"That will do." $catchreleaseRewardCap, handed over in a way that suggests he has done this for things far stranger than a fish.
A woman with salt-cracked hands and an academic's posture is sketching something on a slate and covering it whenever anyone walks past.

options: catchrelease_curator_ask:Ask what she is drawing.

text:
"I keep a tank," she says. "Larger than is sensible. I am told it is a conservation programme, which is what people call a collection when it has a grant attached."

"What I want is $catchreleaseAsk."

She taps the slate. "Either will do. A perfect one teaches you what the species is meant to be. A ruined one teaches you what is happening to it. I have space for both and no preference between them."

"$catchreleaseRewardCap. And I will not ask where."
options:
catchrelease_jobAccept:Agree to stock the tank.
catchrelease_jobDecline:"Not my sort of water."

text: "Keep it wet," she says. "Whichever one you find."
She covers the slate again.
"Still $catchreleaseAsk," she says. "Either sort. I have not become fussier."

She has the tank lid off before the crate is properly open, and does not thank you until everything is in the water.

Then she does, at some length, and pays you $catchreleaseReward.
Two children who should not be in here are conducting negotiations at a corner table. One of them is doing all the talking. The other one has a bucket.

options: catchrelease_duel_ask:Find out what the children want.

text:
"We need two," the loud one says. "For the battle."

The quiet one turns the bucket so you can see into it. There is nothing in the bucket. This does not appear to have discouraged anyone.

"$catchreleaseAskCap. One each. Then they fight."

You point out that they will not fight. This is dismissed as an adult opinion. The payment, when it is produced, is $catchreleaseReward - and it is produced from four pockets, so you understand that it is all of it.
options:
catchrelease_jobAccept:Agree to supply the battle.
catchrelease_jobDecline:Explain, gently, that fish do not fight.

text: The loud one shakes your hand. The quiet one does not, but does nod, which you gather is the binding part.
They take this well, which is somehow worse.
"Have you got them yet." It is the fourth time today for somebody.

You hand the better of the two to $catchreleaseKid. There is a silence of the kind that precedes either delight or a formal complaint.

$catchreleaseOtherCap declares this unfair. The declaration is noted and ignored.

Between them they produce $catchreleaseReward, which they clearly consider a fortune, and which they are not wrong about.

You hand the better of the two to $catchreleaseKid. There is a silence of the kind that precedes either delight or a formal complaint.

It is a serious fish. Both of them go very quiet, and then $catchreleaseOther empties a pocket onto the table without being asked.

Between them they produce $catchreleaseReward, which they clearly consider a fortune, and which they are not wrong about.

text:
"You bring the stock," says the one who introduces himself as $catchreleaseLeft. "We supply the rest." He does not say what the rest is. The other one, $catchreleaseRight, taps the ampoule case on the table, which is an answer of sorts.

"$catchreleaseAskCap. Two, because it is not much of an event with one."

options:

text: Neither of them writes anything down. You get the impression that they will remember.
They go back to watching the room. You are no longer part of what they are watching, which is a relief.
"Still two," one of them says, without turning round.

You take the fee. One of them looks briefly disappointed in you, which from a man in this line of work is close to a compliment.

$catchreleaseRewardCap, counted out on the tank lid.

The tank goes in. Something is added to the water from an unlabelled ampoule. Nobody explains what, and the room leans in.

$catchreleaseWager's fish is still moving. Yours was on it. You are paid $catchreleaseReward, and paid promptly, which is the part that tells you they are serious people.

The tank goes in. Something is added to the water from an unlabelled ampoule. Nobody explains what, and the room leans in.

It is over quickly and it is not your side that it is over for. $catchreleaseFoe shrugs. "You picked. That is the whole of it."

text: A woman at the end of the bar is dressed for somewhere else entirely and is not troubled by this. She has been looking at you for a while, and it is not the look you would assume.

options: catchrelease_client_ask:Find out what she wants.

text:
"I have a client," she says. "That is the word I am going to use and we are both going to leave it there."

"He wants a fish. A real one, out of the water, not off a menu. $catchreleaseAskCap - that is the floor, and I want you to understand that it is a floor."

You ask what it is for. She looks at you with enormous patience.

"$catchreleaseRewardCap," she says. "More if it is bigger. That is the entire arrangement and it is a very good one."
options:
catchrelease_jobAccept:Take the arrangement.
catchrelease_jobDecline:"I don't think so."

text: "Discreetly," she says. "Not secretly. There is a difference and the difference is paperwork."
"Of course." She is already looking past you at the door.
"Still $catchreleaseAsk," she says. "He has not become less specific."

She does not open the container in the bar. She weighs it, in her hands, the way somebody does when they have done it before.

$catchreleaseRewardCap changes hands, and she is gone before you have counted it.

She does not open the container in the bar. She weighs it, in her hands, the way somebody does when they have done it before.

"Oh, that is over," she says. "That is comfortably over."

$catchreleaseRewardCap changes hands, and she is gone before you have counted it.
A researcher with an Academy lanyard she has stopped bothering to hide is working through a stack of sample logs and marking almost all of them as useless.

options: catchrelease_academy_ask:Ask what she is marking.

text:
"Everyone brings me good ones," she says. "Whole ones. Beautiful ones. They are worthless to me and I have stopped being polite about it."

"$catchreleaseAskCap. Barely holding together. If it looks like it is about to stop being a fish, that is the specimen."

She notices your expression. "A stable one tells me what a fish is. I know what a fish is. I want to know what is happening to them, and the ones it is happening to are the ones that come up wrong."

"$catchreleaseRewardCap. The Academy will not ask where either."
options:
catchrelease_jobAccept:Agree to bring her a bad one.
catchrelease_jobDecline:Leave her to it.

text: "Do not stabilise it in transit," she says. "Please. It has happened."
She goes back to marking things useless.
"$catchreleaseAskCap," she says. "Worse is better. I am aware of how that sounds."

She holds it up to the light, and whatever she sees through it makes her sit down.

"Thank you. Genuinely." $catchreleaseRewardCap, and a promise you will be in a footnote.
Somebody has set up two lamps and a very expensive lens pointed at an empty chair, and is explaining to the bar staff that it will only take a minute.

options: catchrelease_tuber_ask:Ask what the lamps are for.

text:
"Do not look at the lens," he says, meaning that you should. "I do fishing content. It is a growing vertical."

"I need $catchreleaseAsk. To hold up. That is the shot - I hold it up, I say the name, people find out fish are real."

"I cannot pay what a buyer pays. What I can do is $catchreleaseReward, all of which was sent to me by people who want to be in a video."
options:
catchrelease_jobAccept:Agree to be in the video.
catchrelease_jobDecline:Step out of the shot.

text: "Amazing. Amazing. Can you say that again with the lamps on?"
"No, that is fair. That is completely fair." He is still filming.
"No rush," he says, in the voice of a man with a posting schedule. "$catchreleaseAskCap."
He films it from four angles and pays you $catchreleaseReward out of a box of things people have sent him.

He films it for a long time and then goes quiet in a way you recognise from people looking at a number that has not moved.

"It did fine," he says. "Fine is the worst thing. Nobody stops for a healthy fish." He looks up. "Can you get me a bad one? On purpose?"

"$catchreleaseAskCap. Something that looks like it is arguing with being alive. $catchreleaseRewardCap, and I will credit you, which I appreciate is not payment."

"That," he says, watching the playback, "is the thumbnail. That is the whole video and I have not shot the video."

$catchreleaseRewardCap, out of a box of things people have sent him.
Three people in matching, unremarkable coats are sharing one drink between them and have not touched it. They are waiting, and they are not impatient.

options: catchrelease_cult_ask:Ask the three in the coats what they are waiting for.

text:
One of them says a name. Not yours - the fish's.

"$catchreleaseSpecies," they repeat, when you do not answer immediately. "One. Whole."

You ask what for. There is a pause of exactly the length of somebody deciding not to be offended, and then the same sentence again, with the same emphasis, as though the problem had been the volume.

"$catchreleaseRewardCap," the second one adds, and produces it, and puts it on the table, and leaves it there while you think about it.
options:
catchrelease_jobAccept:Agree to find it.
catchrelease_jobDecline:Decline, politely.

text: None of them thanks you. All three of them nod at the same time, which is worse.
They do not seem to mind. You get the strong impression they will be here when you come back.
"$catchreleaseSpecies," one of them says. That is the whole of the conversation.

They do not open it. One of them puts a hand flat on the lid and leaves it there for rather too long.

$catchreleaseRewardCap, pushed across the table. Nobody says what it is for, and by now you have stopped expecting them to.

notes: They open the link themselves the first time and never again - being asked once is a distress call and being asked on every pass is a toll. Unprefixed keys because there is no active person at this trigger.

10:catchrelease_fqDecline:Decline
notes: The pitch is read off the fleet's own memory so one row serves every kind of trouble it could be in.

text: They send over what little they know about the local water and settle in to wait. Whatever else happens out here they will be exactly where you left them.
They take it the way anyone takes it. The link closes without anything further being said - and they are still going to be here.
notes: Declining does not end the job. The fleet is pinned either way and the offer stands the next time the player calls.

text: They are exactly where you left them and they have not stopped watching the water.

options: 0:catchrelease_fqTurnIn:Hand over the catch
notes: The option exists only when the hold can pay for it - updateData counts it and the flag it sets is what this row is really asking about.

options: 10:catchrelease_fqLeave:Leave them to it

text: The crates go across without ceremony. Somebody aboard says something that does not come through cleanly and several other people laugh at it.
The link closes. They go back to waiting.

AddText "The $faction $otherShipOrFleet comes alongside without hurrying, and hails you." $faction.baseColor

notes: A holed crew that has come to be paid rather than to fight. Unprefixed keys because there is no active person at this trigger, which puts the fleet's own memory in the local scope. The done flag is a day rather than the patrol's thirty: this is not enforcement, so a player who breaks off is hailed again next time rather than never again - the day is only there to stop the encounter reopening the comm the instant it is closed. Paying or refusing sets the long one through the command.

text:
"You are the one with the rope." It is not a question, and $PersonRank $personName does not sound angry so much as tired of the shift.

"We are not the navy and we are not going to pretend we are. There is a hole in a hull that was surveyed clean this morning, and somebody has to pay a yard to close it. $entity.catchrelease_harpoonDamagesDGS credits and we log it as debris."

text: "Right." $PersonRank $personName reads something off a screen, nods at it, and cuts the link without another word. The $otherShipOrFleet peels away and goes back to its heading.
notes: Paying the people you holed closes the faction's books as well, which is the whole point of settling with them - nobody else comes asking about a hole already paid for. The flags are given a day rather than a zero, because a rules assignment with a zero on it expires on the first unpaused frame and the script that reads it back does not run until then. The global one is what tells that script to go looking at all.

text:
There is a pause on the other end that goes on slightly too long.

"Noted," $PersonRank $personName says, and writes something down. The link closes and the $otherShipOrFleet holds its heading, which is somehow worse than if it had not.
notes: Nothing happens to the player here and nothing happens to the crew - a hauler has no enforcement behind it. It goes in the report instead, which is filed as an evasion and charged in reputation a few days later, out of sight of the conversation.
